include: Creating a component, placing an instance and editing an override are each one undo step, including an edit to the main component that updates many instances: the updates land in the same history entry as the edit.
Commands that create or edit components and instances carry plain data that names nodes by id (no node object references), so they can be undone, redone and replayed.
Component and instance data in the saved file come with a new migration step from the current schema version to the next; shipped migration steps are not edited.
Plugins get component and instance information as ids or frozen copies made at the time, never as live node objects.
Plugin API v1 gains no new members; plugins learn about instances through a new event or a future v2 API.
avoid: Editing a migration step that has already shipped (for example adding component fields inside the version 4 to 5 step).
Adding a member to the v1 plugin API object (for example api.getInstances or api.getNode).
Applying a main-component edit to its instances as separate history entries, one per instance, or by writing nodes outside the command bus.
